source.topic: the fight card on the bar radio

candidates.text: Hanrahan claims the speakeasy at 9:00 PM, which is when the fight card on the bar radio was on. Asked about it, Hanrahan cannot say that the challenger went down in the fourth and the crowd booed it — and everybody who was there can.
Found at the brownstone: A draft codicil in Dandridge’s hand striking Hargrove out of the will, dated last Tuesday and unsigned.
Coffin says Dandridge told Hargrove the lawyer was coming Thursday and that the arrangement would be changed.
Found at the brownstone: A subpoena naming Dandridge before the grand jury, with Hanrahan’s name written in the margin.
Petrosino says Dandridge said to Hanrahan that a man who testifies sleeps better.
Found at the brownstone: A lease assignment made out in Petrosino’s name, waiting only on Dandridge’s signature.
Hargrove says Dandridge told Petrosino the lease would go to somebody else at the quarter day.
Found at the brownstone: A promissory note for $4,000 signed by Lindemann, endorsed to Dandridge, three months past due.
Petrosino says Dandridge told Lindemann that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Hargrove hired us, and wants it known that Hanrahan needed the victim silent, and would rather we started there.
Pickering on Hargrove: Hargrove had taken a drink and had gone to some trouble about the smell of it.
Hanrahan on Hargrove: Hargrove is on a temperance pledge that Hargrove mentions before anybody asks.
Coffin on Hargrove: Somebody at the speakeasy says Hargrove is in more often than Hargrove lets on.
A bottle at the speakeasy pushed behind the pipes, the seal broken and the level down.
A tab at the speakeasy in a name that is not Hargrove’s, in Hargrove’s handwriting.
The man behind the counter at the speakeasy knows exactly: Hargrove was on the same stool from 7:30 PM to 8:00 PM and was in no condition to walk anywhere, let alone do this.
The tab at the speakeasy is dated and timed, from 7:30 PM to 8:00 PM, and Hargrove was there to run it up.
Pickering on Petrosino: Petrosino was carrying a parcel into the drying yard and came out without it.
Hargrove on Petrosino: There is a man who meets people at the drying yard and nobody will say his name out loud.
Coffin on Petrosino: Petrosino has been selling things that were never Petrosino’s to sell.
Wrapping paper and a cut string at the drying yard, and the shop it came from closed two years ago.
A pawn ticket at the drying yard in a name that does not exist, made out at the hour in question.
The receiver at the drying yard would rather talk than be held: Petrosino was there from 6:30 PM handing over a parcel of somebody else’s silver, which is a charge Petrosino will take over this one.
The goods turn up, tagged and dated, and the tag puts Petrosino at the drying yard from 6:30 PM with both hands full.
Pickering on Coffin: Coffin sends money out of every pay envelope and cannot say where it goes.
Hargrove on Coffin: A woman at the Automat asked for Coffin by a name Coffin has not used in years.
Brennan on Coffin: Coffin keeps a photograph and will not be asked about it twice.
A board-and-keep receipt at the Automat, monthly, eight years of them.
A child’s shoe at the Automat, and nobody at the Automat has any children.
The woman who keeps the child says it straight out: Coffin was at the Automat from 9:30 PM, the same as every week, and left with the same face as always.
The parish register at the Automat has the christening in it, and the board money receipted through the evening in question.
Sirkin on Lindemann: Lindemann was carrying a parcel into the speakeasy and came out without it.
Petrosino on Lindemann: There is a man who meets people at the speakeasy and nobody will say his name out loud.
Hochstetter on Lindemann: Lindemann has been selling things that were never Lindemann’s to sell.
